messages:
maya: getting a spike of 401s from multiple customers starting ~11:12 UTC. Hits on /v1/generate and /v1/chat, mainly eu-west and us-central. Customers reporting immediate failures after yesterday's key rotation rollout.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0831A (auth-service degraded) — paging oncall.

maya: logs show introspect returning 403 for many tokens. Quick grep: `introspect: token_id=acct_*** status=not_found` — but the signing keys look present on the control plane.

ishaan: I see rotation job ran at 03:10 UTC and backfill started at 03:12. Backfill job errored with transient DB timeouts, retried, then marked complete. Could be a propagation gap.

alice: Customer repro steps from support: 1) POST /v1/auth with api_key header 2) 200 OK token 3) subsequent POST to /v1/chat returns 401 after ~30s. Attached snippet: ````
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
=> 401 {"error":"invalid_token","message":"token not recognized"}
````

sam: Are we seeing KV cache evictions on auth cache replicas? Metrics show a small but sharp increase in cache misses around 11:10.

maya: yes, cache-miss rate went from 0.3% to 8% in the window. I also see the key-backfill process writing to the postgres signing_keys table but some cache nodes didn't pick up the change — likely due to a concurrency bug in the cache invalidation path.

ishaan: quick mitigation: rolling restart of auth-cache pods in eu-west and us-central to force rehydrate. Starting now.

support-engineer: PS — field support is getting multiple tickets. We should enable a temporary graceful fallback to legacy-introspect (non-cache path) for high-error customers. Can we toggle a flag?

alice: we have a feature flag `auth.fallback_on_cache_failure` in prod. It's off by default. I can flip it for the affected orgs, but need a list of org IDs. Sam can we export top-error orgs?

sam: exporting now -> sending list to #private-support. Also adding an automated rule to route those orgs to the legacy path until full fix.

oncall-bot: Deploy job started: auth-cache roll restart eu-west (podset-3) — tracking at https://deploys.redwood.ai/12345

maya: after restart, 401 error rate dropped ~90% in eu-west within 2 minutes. us-central still has a high tail, continuing restarts.

ishaan: root cause hypothesis: backfill job used a batched invalidation logic that assumed TTLs were aligned across pods; DB retries caused partial completion leading to stale cache entries in some replicas. I'll open a PR to make invalidation idempotent and add a verification pass.

alice: short-term checklist: 1) flip `auth.fallback_on_cache_failure` for affected orgs (done for 8 orgs) 2) finish roll restart across regions (in progress) 3) monitor error-rate -> aim <0.5% for 30m before closing.

maya: notifying CSMs and adding notes to status.redwood.ai. Internal postmortem assigned to ishaan + alice + infra.

support-engineer: customers updated. Affected customers requested root-cause details and ETA for full fix. We'll coordinate on the postmortem before public messaging.

ishaan: PR reference: https://git.redwood.ai/r/auth/+/PR-2424 (invalidations: make idempotent + add verification pass). Planning to deploy canary to staging tonight, then prod next window.

maya: thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with metrics. If anyone sees a regression after restarts, ping here with a sample request id. :thumbsup:
